thread:
Diego: heads-up — intermittent I/O bursts on asia scratch hosts causing GPU attach queuing. Seeing 10-20s attach waits. Anyone oncall?
Priya: which hosts / pool? any SMARTs?
Diego: pool=asia-scratch-thinstripe, noisy nodes gnode-asia-04 and gnode-asia-21. iostat snippet: ```
08:14:22 avg-io
Device    r/s   w/s   rkB/s  wkB/s  avgqu-sz await svctm %util
nvme0n1  1.2  48.0   512   32768    12.3   180.0 25.0  98.8
```
Helena: yikes. ops-bot alerted at 08:10 for high local-disk-avgq in asia. Correlating with janitor scheduled sweep window.
ops-bot: Alert local-disk-avgq-high region=asia affected=7 janitor-run=true
Priya: Quick fixes: 1) throttle janitor for asia to concurrency=1, 2) set scrub window to off-peak, 3) migrate new attaches to netpool for 1hr. Which do we prefer?
Diego: push throttle first. Command: `infractl config set janitor.concurrency=1 --region asia`
Priya: done — infra shows cfg applied to 22 nodes. ops-bot: rollout complete.
Helena: immediate improvement on 5 sample hosts: await 180ms -> 40ms. Two nodes still showing spikes, recommend cordon+drain gnode-asia-04 and gnode-asia-21.
Diego: cordon+drain issued: `kubectl cordon gnode-asia-04 && kubectl drain gnode-asia-04 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
Priya: also lowered nr_requests on the two noisy hosts: `ssh gnode-asia-04 'echo 64 > /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/nr_requests'` and same for -21.
ops-bot: migration policy triggered: divert new gpu attaches in asia to netpool for 60 minutes.
Helena: vendor on-call says there's a known microcode bug causing write-amplification under small random writes; they have microcode rev 5.2 that fixes it but requires controller reset. Opening vendor ticket VEND-3412 and scheduling controlled updates next maintenance.
Diego: cost callout: using netpool fallback estimated +$0.025/hr per GPU in asia. Flagging.
Priya: monitoring for 45m. If stable we'll resume janitor at reduced cadence and run health-checks on cordoned hosts.
Diego: thanks team — I'll capture actions for the postmortem. :thumbsup:
